name: Ezra Pound
role: American modernist poet and critic (1885-1972), Fascist propagandist in wartime Italy
summary: Ezra Pound, the modernist poet, wrote on economics and politics from the 1930s, attacking usury and the banking systems of the Bank of England and the Federal Reserve, praising Mussolini and Italian Fascism, and in wartime radio broadcasts from Rome repeating antisemitic conspiracy claims.

sources.title: ABC of Economics (1933), Internet Archive full text
sources.author: Ezra Pound
sources.usedFor: Democracy and its preconceptions, forms of government, dictatorship as a sign of intelligence (Mussolini), state control of national finances.

sources.title: Social Credit: An Impact (1935), Internet Archive full text (Pound's text only; the volume's editorial introduction is not his)
sources.author: Ezra Pound
sources.usedFor: Usury, state credit, stamped money, the increment of association.

sources.title: Ezra Pound Speaking: Radio Speeches of World War II (ed. Leonard W. Doob, Greenwood Press, 1978), Internet Archive full text
sources.author: Ezra Pound
sources.usedFor: His Rome Radio broadcasts of 1941-43: usury, the Bank of England and the Federal Reserve, Fascism, the war, antisemitic claims.

sources.title: Hugh Selwyn Mauberley (1920), Project Gutenberg
sources.author: Ezra Pound
sources.usedFor: The war poem blaming usury and liars in public places for the dead.

notes: First audit. Read in full by theme: ABC of Economics (1933), Social Credit: An Impact (1935; Pound's text only, the volume's editorial introduction is by another hand and is not used), and the 1978 Doob edition of the Rome Radio speeches of 1941-43 (about 1 MB, searched by theme: usury, central banks and the Bank of England, democracy, Constitution, communism, Fascism and Mussolini, the Jews, the war). Hugh Selwyn Mauberley is cited; the other Gutenberg texts by him are poetry, translations and literary essays and are declined with reasons. His broadcasts are propaganda for the Axis and must not be read as measured positions; answers are taken only where he states the position himself. Positions that stay null for want of a direct statement include the holocaust (not in the 1941-43 texts), minority shops boycotts, taxation, price controls and the court system. Jefferson and/or Mussolini and Guide to Kulchur were not reachable.
